title: Per-route margin lighthouse scenario — Q3 2026
body:
Purpose:
This working sheet models a per-route (per-API-route) view of unit economics and headcount staging for a Q3 2026 lighthouse experiment: apply differentiated pricing + latency SLAs to three customer cohorts and measure margin sensitivity. This doc bundles a compact budget projection, hiring triggers, and pricing sensitivity outputs for product + serving runtime tradeoffs.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Goal: Validate whether a small set of per-route price bands tied to latency SLOs and batch/caching profiles can increase realized gross margin by ~8–12% with minimal additional hires.
- Baseline monthly run-rate (hosted): $3.1M revenue, token COGS ~ $1.65M, gross margin 46.8%.
- Target after experiment (mid case): revenue up 6% (mix shift to higher-tier routes), COGS down 4% through improved batching and caching on high-volume routes, gross margin ~55%.
- Key ask: runway for +6 FTEs (engineering + SRE + product) staged across 3 sprints; stop-gap if margin improvement <4% after 8 weeks.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Volume assumed steady-state for base scenario: 9.2B tokens/month across hosted customers in scope.
- Cost per GPU-minute & inference infra growth baked into COGS; we model per-token COGS bands by route type.
- Price bands: Base (current avg price), Mid (+12%), Premium (+30%) for routes with 99th percentile latency <120ms.
- Hiring: Avg fully-burdened cost per FTE = $26.5k/mo (incl benefits/ops).
- Time horizon: 3-month experiment window, with annualized projection column to compare steady-state effect.

Scenario definitions:
1) Baseline: current product mix & prices (no per-route gating).
2) Mid-case (experiment): Introduce 3 price bands, selective routing optimizations on top 10% of routes by volume.
3) Upside: aggressive migration of mid-volume routes to optimized path + wider adoption of premium tier (customer negotiation wins).
4) Downside: price elasticity causes 10% volume loss on premium tier; optimizations take longer (12 weeks).

Budget snapshot (experiment months Apr–Jun 2026) — simplified ledger:
| Category                      | Apr (k$) | May (k$) | Jun (k$) | Q2 total (k$) | Annualized est (k$) | Notes |
|------------------------------|---------:|--------:|--------:|-------------:|--------------------:|------|
| Hosted revenue (baseline)    | 3100     | 3150    | 3180    | 9430         | 37800               | baseline run-rate
| COGS (inference infra)       | 1650     | 1620    | 1600    | 4870         | 19500               | includes spot + reserved estimate
| Gross margin                 | 1450     | 1530    | 1580    | 4560         | 18300               | 46.8% baseline avg
| Experiment incremental spend | 0        | 85      | 115     | 200          | 800                 | tooling, perf lab, consulting
| Incremental headcount cost   | 0        | 53      | 106     | 159          | 636                 | hires staged in May/Jun (3 eng, 1 sre, 1 product)
| Net contribution (post-exp) | 1450     | 1392    | 1359    | 4201         | 16964               | conservative after hires

Headcount plan (staging plan tied to experiment):
| Role                       | Hires planned | Start month | FTE monthly cost (k$) | Notes |
|---------------------------|--------------:|------------|---------------------:|------|
| Serving runtime engineer  | 2             | May        | 26.5                 | focus on prefix caching + kernel tuning
| SRE (inference infra)     | 1             | May        | 26.5                 | deployment & rollbacks, capacity policies
| Product manager (pricing) | 1             | Jun        | 26.5                 | pricing ops, customer experiments
| Data analyst (observability)| 1           | Jun        | 18.2                 | evals, A/B metric instrumentation
| Total incremental FTEs     | 5             | May–Jun    |                      | staged hires, contract-first if risk arises

Per-route pricing sensitivity (condensed matrix) — mid experiment window
Assumptions: split of volume by route band: Base 65%, Mid 25%, Premium 10% (by tokens).
| Price delta | Volume delta (tokens) | Revenue delta (%) | COGS delta (%) | Gross margin delta (pp) | Notes |
|-----------:|-----------------------:|-------------------:|---------------:|------------------------:|------|
| -15%       | +3% (elasticity low)   | -12%               | -4%            | -8.2                    | price-led churn on base
| 0% (baseline)| 0%                   | 0%                 | 0%             | 0                       | 
| +12% (mid) | -4%                    | +6%                | -2%            | +5.6                    | customers accept mid tier
| +30% (prem)| -9%                    | +12%               | -5%            | +9.8                    | premium concentrated on SLA routes

Interpretation notes: a moderate +12% mid band lifted margin materially because COGS per-token for optimized routes drops via higher batching and cache hit rates. Premium (+30%) shows highest margin lift but risk of volume loss — depends on how many customers can meet latency SLOs.

Sensitivity graphs (described for sheet tabs):
- Tab: price_vs_margin: sweep price adjustments [-20%, +40%] and compute revenue & margin bands at 3 elasticity curves (inelastic, base, elastic).
- Tab: headcount_trigger: model hires v. margin threshold; binary stop/hire decisions.

Hiring triggers and stop conditions (operational runbook):
- Hire stage 1 (2 eng, 1 sre) if within 4 weeks: rolling improvement in margin >= 4% and 95th pct latency improvements >= 10% on targeted routes.
- Hire stage 2 (1 PM, 1 analyst) if after 8 weeks: conversion to mid/premium tiers shows sustained revenue lift >= 3% month-over-month.
- Abort/rollback: if after 8 weeks net margin improvement < 2% or premium volume lost > 12% and ARR impact > $1.2M annualized, freeze hires and revert pricing for top 5 affected customers.

Sensitivity summary table (decision-friendly):
| Trigger check                        | Action if true                       | Action if false |
|-------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|-----------------|
| Margin uplift >= 4% at week 4       | Proceed to stage 1 hires             | Pause, deeper root-cause analysis
| Premium adoption >= 6% of premium-eligible | Unlock stage 2 PM & analyst      | Keep customer-specific pilots
| Net ARR delta < -$100k after 8 weeks| Rollback premium band for affected accounts | Continue experiment

Open questions / items to close before go/no-go:
- Exact contract language for per-route SLO credits (legal) — tradeoffs and SLA credit calculation (see linked ticket ENG-8721).
- Measurement: final metric to measure success = realized gross margin across instrumented routes (not list price margin). Need instrumentation ownership (observability team).
- Sales ops: playbook for customer negotiations for premium tier discounts vs commitment.

Recommendation (next steps):
1) Approve $200k experiment budget for May–Jun to cover tooling, consulting, and early hiring (as above).
2) Kick off 4-week perf audit on top 10% routes by tokens (serving runtime + SRE owners).
3) Prepare pricing playbook + legal SLA draft; run 3 pilot customers in May.
4) Reevaluate at 8-week checkpoint against the hiring triggers and margin thresholds above.

Notes to reviewer: this is a working sheet — numbers are intentionally rounded and will be replaced by the detailed sheet tabs (price_vs_margin, headcount_trigger, ledger). Prefer to keep hires contract-first if downside risk increases.

End of doc.
